context: Current closing price of Union Pacific (UNP): $264.48 USD as of 2026-06-02.
justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a broadly stable outlook with a slight upward drift over time. At the one-day horizon, I anchored close to the prevailing price level, assuming mean-reversion tendencies dominate over such a short window and that no major catalysts were imminent. The one-week estimate nudges marginally higher, reflecting a modest positive drift assumption consistent with long-run equity risk premium dynamics. The one-month estimate extends that drift a bit further, though the increment remains small because I did not want to overstate directional conviction over a period where macroeconomic crosscurrents could easily dominate any trend signal.

The confidence interval widths widen appropriately as the horizon extends, driven by the compounding of daily volatility. At the one-day level, a roughly plus-or-minus six-point range captures typical intraday-to-next-day variability for an instrument in this price range, consistent with realized volatility in the low-to-mid single-digit percentage annualized range translated to a daily sigma. By one week, the interval nearly doubles in half-width, reflecting the square-root-of-time scaling of uncertainty. At one month, the interval widens considerably further, incorporating not just volatility scaling but also the possibility of regime shifts in monetary policy expectations, earnings surprises, or geopolitical developments that could structurally reprice the underlying.

The primary sources of uncertainty I weighted include Federal Reserve communication and interest rate path revisions, incoming macroeconomic data such as inflation prints and employment reports, and broader risk appetite shifts that could compress or expand equity multiples. Liquidity conditions and positioning dynamics also play a role, particularly at shorter horizons where technical flows can dominate fundamentals.

Events that could push outcomes outside my stated intervals include a surprise central bank policy shift, an unexpected geopolitical escalation, or a systemic financial stress event such as a credit market dislocation. On the upside, a stronger-than-expected resolution of trade or geopolitical tensions, or a surprisingly dovish policy pivot, could push prices well above my upper bounds. These tail risks are real but were not assigned high enough probability to widen the intervals further without overfitting to speculative scenarios.
